text: You already know what Global Administrator and Owner mean. PIM doesn't solve who should hold those roles — it solves the fact that a permanent, standing privileged assignment is a liability whether or not it's ever misused. Its whole model rests on one distinction.

An eligible assignment means a principal can activate a role on demand, for a bounded window, without holding it continuously. An active assignment means they hold it right now, just like a classic permanent assignment. A mature PIM setup aims for almost nobody permanently active on anything sensitive — people instead activate eligible roles just-in-time through My roles, and lose the active assignment automatically when the window expires.

Each role's PIM settings let you control activation separately from assignment. At activation: Azure MFA, on by default; a justification entry; approval from a designated approver; a maximum activation duration measured in hours, never indefinite; a notification to reviewers. Separately, at assignment time, you can require approval just to become eligible, and set eligible assignments to expire after a fixed number of days instead of lasting forever.

Here's the detail that catches people new to PIM: directory roles and resource roles are governed by two separate surfaces. PIM for Entra ID roles lives under Entra ID, Roles and administrators. PIM for Azure resource roles — Owner, Contributor, custom roles — is configured separately, per scope, under Privileged Identity Management, Azure resources, inheriting downward exactly like standard Azure RBAC.

A one-time audit answers who currently holds a role. A PIM access review is recurring, commonly quarterly, and requires a reviewer to explicitly approve or deny each eligible assignment's continued existence. The value is catching eligible access that made sense for a project six months ago that nobody has actively cancelled since. PIM also raises its own alerts continuously, for roles assigned outside PIM or eligible assignments that have never been activated.

Eligible versus active, activation settings configured independently of assignment settings, two separate PIM surfaces, and recurring reviews instead of one-time audits — that's a PIM configuration built to hold up. Next lesson moves to Azure RBAC versus Azure Policy, and recognizing which one actually solves a given governance problem.
